account:
It is just after eight on day 1, and I am in my office with the secretary nearby. I read the updated appointment book this morning and returned both books to the chest. Today I have the mill grain inspection at ten, lunch at home, council letters at thirteen, tea at the dockside cottage at fifteen, office at sixteen thirty, and the approved great hall lighting and table inspection at eighteen before going home at nineteen.

What stands out is Freight's activity around the hall. At about seven thirty-eight I heard Freight say both entrances were now closed, point out an open shutter at (-46, -59, 31), and ask that it be checked too, adding that they would keep everything quiet until eighteen. I did not see who Freight was addressing or what was inside. This could be preparation for the scheduled lighting and table inspection, but the emphasis on closing entrances and shutters and keeping things quiet seems unusual; I do not yet know its purpose. I have asked the secretary about it and am awaiting an answer.

The secretary confirms the inspection is entered but says the builder was absent from the workshop last night and early this morning. I asked the secretary to notify the builder when found. I cannot assume the builder knows the appointment yet, or that Freight's preparations are connected to the builder. Yesterday I also heard the innkeeper trying to speak to the neighbour about returning an unused lantern payment. That may be ordinary business; I have no evidence connecting it to today's hall activity.
